tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact format moves = [[disk_id, from_peg, to_peg], ...] so the parser can extract it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have finished determining the required moves and are ready to respond.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing no move list or placing extra commentary after the list, causing the parser to miss the moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you need to move is not the topmost disk on its peg, first relocate the smaller disks that sit above it, typically using recursion, before moving the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a desired move involves a disk that has smaller disks on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 while disks 1, 2, 3 remain on top of it, resulting in an illegal source‑top mismatch.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Consolidate all disks onto a single source peg before applying classic Hanoi recursion
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the initial configuration spreads the movable disks across multiple pegs, first move the smaller disks onto one empty peg so that the entire stack to be transferred resides on a single source peg; then apply the standard recursive Hanoi algorithm.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: If the disks that need to be moved are not already stacked on a single peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Applying the recursive Hanoi steps while disks are split between two pegs, causing illegal moves because the source stack is not contiguous.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk, check that the destination peg is either empty or its topmost disk is larger than the moving disk; otherwise the move would violate the size rule.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 2 onto a peg whose top disk is 1, which is smaller, resulting in an illegal placement.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Keep answer concise and place move list at the very end
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer parser reads the last parseable list in the response; any text after the move list is ignored, so the move list should be the final content and no extra commentary should follow.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending explanatory sentences after the move list, causing the parser to stop reading before the list ends.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg; if it is not, first move the blocking smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 from a peg where disk 1 is on top, leading to a source‑top mismatch.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move n disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, recursively move n‑1 disks to the auxiliary, move the nth disk to the target, then move the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary to the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have a single contiguous stack of n disks on a source peg and need to transfer it to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Generating a move list that does not follow the recursive pattern, resulting in an incorrect final configuration.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops before emitting the moves, often due to premature termination or forgetting to output the list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate and place a complete move list before ending the response.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops early, cutting off the list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the move sequence to fit within the token budget, or break the solution into concise steps; ensure the list is complete before the response ends.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk based on goal position without checking the current stack order.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the chosen disk is on top; if not, first move the blocking smaller disks.
